title: Which electroweak multiplets can be inelastic dark matter with a 100-400 keV neutral splitting?
question: For SU(2)_L fermion multiplets (n,Y) with a neutral component, which have a Z vector coupling (Y != 0), how is the Majorana splitting delta generated and at what scale Lambda, what delta gives one LZ event for Y = 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, and how does it compare with P007/P021?
headline_result: Every Y != 0 multiplet scatters like the Higgsino with sigma_n = 7.4e-39 (2Y)^2 cm^2 and fits the LZ event at delta = 365.8/374.1/379.2/382.7 keV (Y = 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2; 1 TeV; all inside P021's 360-385 keV band); the splitting operator chi chi (H^dag)^(4Y)/Lambda^(4Y-1) needs Lambda = 1.66e5 TeV (= 4 M1/g'^2 of P007 to 1%), 21.6 TeV, 3.6 TeV, 1.7 TeV, so only the doublet and the Y = 1 triplet have a consistent heavy-mediator origin; Y = 0 multiplets cannot scatter
model_or_mechanism: SU(2)_L x U(1)_Y fermion multiplets n=2-5 with neutral component; Z-vector inelastic O1 with (2Y)^2 scaling of P007 Higgsino couplings on P007 WimPyDD grid; dimension-(3+4Y) Majorana-splitting operators; one-loop Cirelli-Fornengo-Strumia charged-neutral splittings
result_type: computed (cross-sections, Lambda, delta(N), splittings); estimated (thermal masses, ctau)
agent_tools: Read x16, Bash x9, Write x4, Edit x7, Skill x1 (dataviz)
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (quad, erf/erfc, brentq); pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (eft_hamiltonian, diff_rate via lzcommon); common/lzcommon.py
